name: Communication & Public Speaking

objectives.text: Identify the introduction, body, and conclusion of a simple prepared speech
Demonstrate active listening by summarizing the main idea and one supporting detail of a classmate's short talk
Explain how eye contact, posture, voice volume, and gestures help a speaker connect with an audience
Deliver a one to two minute informative talk about a farm animal, crop, or natural resource to classmates
Organize an outline for a short speech on an agricultural topic with a clear main idea, supporting points, and a closing statement
Explain the meaning of each paragraph of the FFA Creed in your own words
Describe how a speaker adjusts word choice and examples for different audiences such as peers, younger students, and community members
Deliver the FFA Creed from memory with accurate wording, clear pronunciation, and expressive delivery
Respond to judges' questions about a speech or the FFA Creed with clear, concise, and relevant answers
Distinguish among forms of verbal communication used in agriculture such as public speaking, presentations, debate, radio, and podcasts
Explain why strong verbal communication matters for agricultural careers, SAE growth, and agricultural advocacy
Identify strategies such as vocal variety, logical organization, eye contact, and thorough preparation that make spoken communication clear and professional
Analyze a target audience to select the purpose, key message, and supporting evidence for an agricultural presentation
Research an agricultural topic using credible sources and cite them accurately in a prepared speech manuscript
Write and deliver a six to eight minute prepared speech on an agricultural topic that meets FFA Prepared Public Speaking CDE guidelines
Analyze a recorded speech for clarity, organization, nonverbal delivery, and persuasive appeal
Design visual aids that support rather than distract from an oral presentation of SAE records and results
Demonstrate professional interview skills for an agricultural job, proficiency award, or FFA degree interview
Plan and deliver an extemporaneous speech on a current agricultural issue with limited preparation time
Present multiple perspectives on a controversial agricultural issue and respond respectfully to challenging questions in an issues forum
Develop a communication plan that combines speaking opportunities with other media to promote a chapter event or SAE to an intended audience
Create a communication plan for answering public questions and criticism about an agricultural practice
Deliver a persuasive presentation advocating an agricultural position to a public audience such as a school board, civic club, or elected official
Evaluate and coach a peer's speech using official FFA CDE speaking rubrics

changes: Removed the confession reference so scripture and confessions are empty for every objective. Kept and reworded all six original competencies. Added foundational listening, delivery, and outlining skills for grades 4 to 6, FFA Creed understanding, delivery, and questioning for grades 7 to 8, and high school competencies for audience analysis, research and citation, visual aids, interviews, issues forums, communication planning, responding to criticism, and public advocacy. Each is tagged only with fitting AFNR codes from the candidate list, and objectives below grade 9 have no standards.
